provenance.citation: Downey-Fellows 1999 (DOMINATING SET is W[2]-complete for the solution-size parameter); Hsu-Nemhauser 1979 (the unit-length k-center reduction)
provenance.note: W[2]-hardness of k-means by k is LOGGED here (R20 — the S5 specimen's load-bearing property made explicit, not left implicit-via-Guha-Khuller): DOMINATING SET (W[2]-complete) reduces to k-center/k-median/k-means by giving each graph edge unit length, so a size-k dominating set exists IFF k centers achieve cost 0 (every point coincides with a chosen center iff it is dominated); a no-instance forces cost >= 1, a gap the sum-of-squared-distances objective preserves. The reduction is parameter-preserving in k, so k-means inherits W[2]-hardness. Poly-time constant-factor approximation coexists (see the approximation cell) — the violation.
